title: Android Automotive
description: Android Automotive OS: Car APIs, CarService, UX restrictions, users, audio, power and system UI.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Android Automotive OS (AAOS) and Android Auto?

answers.text: AAOS runs directly on the vehicle's head unit; Android Auto projects apps from a phone
Android Auto runs on the head unit; AAOS runs on the phone
They are the same product with different names

questions.explanation: AAOS is a full Android platform in the car. Android Auto renders phone apps on the car display.

questions.question: Which API do apps use to read vehicle properties such as speed or gear?

answers.text: Direct AIDL calls to the VHAL

questions.explanation: Apps obtain Car via Car.createCar(context) and use CarPropertyManager. Only CarService talks to the VHAL.

questions.question: Which permission is needed to read the vehicle speed via CarPropertyManager?
questions.explanation: Each vehicle property is protected by a car permission. PERF_VEHICLE_SPEED requires CAR_SPEED.

questions.question: What does CarUxRestrictionsManager provide?

answers.text: The current UX restrictions, e.g. limited text or no video while driving
The list of apps the user may install

questions.explanation: UX restrictions are derived from the driving state; apps must adapt their UI to reduce distraction.

questions.question: How does an activity declare that it may be shown while the car is moving?
questions.explanation: Only distraction-optimized activities are allowed in restricted driving states; others are blocked.

questions.question: What is the 'headless system user mode' in AAOS?

answers.text: User 0 runs in the background only; the driver uses a secondary user in the foreground
The car boots without any display
Apps run without a user context

questions.explanation: Since Android 10, AAOS uses a headless system user so that multiple drivers/passengers can have own users.

questions.question: How are third-party media apps integrated in AAOS?

answers.text: Via MediaBrowserService and MediaSession; the system media UI renders them
Each app draws its own full-screen UI

questions.explanation: The car's media center browses the app's MediaBrowserService and controls playback via MediaSession.

questions.question: Which mechanisms let OEMs customize the look of system apps without changing their code?

answers.text: Patching the APK at runtime via the VHAL

questions.explanation: RROs replace resources at runtime; car-ui-lib provides customizable UI components for consistency.

questions.question: Which component provides the status bar and navigation bars (top, bottom, left, right) in AAOS?
questions.explanation: CarSystemUI is the automotive variant of SystemUI and supports system bars on all four sides.

questions.question: What is CarOccupantZoneManager used for?

answers.text: Mapping occupants (driver, passengers) to displays, users and audio zones

questions.explanation: Occupant zones connect displays, users and audio zones, which is key for multi-display setups.

questions.question: How is audio routing configured for audio zones in AAOS?

answers.text: car_audio_configuration.xml together with the audio policy configuration
Each app selects the amplifier channel itself

questions.explanation: Car audio zones group output devices (historically BUS devices) and map audio usages to volume groups.

questions.question: What is Garage Mode?

answers.text: A phase after ignition off in which idle jobs (e.g. updates) can run before suspend

questions.explanation: CarPowerManager enters Garage Mode during SHUTDOWN_PREPARE so JobScheduler idle jobs can run.

questions.question: Which manager lets system components react to power state changes such as suspend?
questions.explanation: Listeners get states like SHUTDOWN_PREPARE, SUSPEND_ENTER and resume events.

questions.question: What is EVS (Extended View System) for?

answers.text: Fast-starting camera views, e.g. rear-view camera, independent of the full Android stack

questions.explanation: EVS can show the rear camera early during boot, which is required by regulations in many markets.

questions.question: What does Car Watchdog monitor?

answers.text: Health of critical processes and services
Disk I/O overuse by apps and services
The driver's attention via the camera

questions.explanation: Car Watchdog kills unresponsive processes and can act on I/O overuse to protect flash memory.

questions.question: You register a CarPropertyManager callback for an ON_CHANGE property with rate 10 Hz. What happens?

answers.text: The rate is ignored; events come when the value changes

questions.explanation: Sample rates only apply to CONTINUOUS properties, within their min/max sample rate.

questions.question: Which library is used to build templated third-party apps (e.g. navigation, POI, IoT) for cars?
questions.explanation: The Car App Library uses templates so the host can render safe UIs on Android Auto and AAOS.

questions.question: Where are the IDs of standard vehicle properties defined for apps?
questions.explanation: VehiclePropertyIds mirrors the VHAL property IDs, e.g. PERF_VEHICLE_SPEED, GEAR_SELECTION.

questions.question: Which statements about CarService are correct?

answers.text: It is the bridge between car APIs used by apps and the Vehicle HAL
It enforces car permissions for vehicle properties
It is a library linked into every app process

questions.explanation: CarService runs in its own process; apps talk to it via Binder through the android.car APIs.

questions.question: What does the Car API method Car.createCar(context) return?

answers.text: A Car object used to obtain car managers via getCarManager()

questions.explanation: From the Car object you get managers like CarPropertyManager, CarAudioManager, CarPowerManager.
